sanitizationReport.fingerprintConvention: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass), with no entryPoint on any finding (this is a /full-audit contract scan; entryPoint is reserved for /audit-script npm entry points). findings.title: Neither the on-chain Unprofitable check nor harvest.sh's minEthOut floor prices the claim NFT burned by SYA; default config sends net-loss harvests
findings.rootCause: Profitability floor = gas only (on-chain (g0-gasleft+60k)*tx.gasprice; script gasLimit*maxFee + MIN_PROFIT_WEI default 0). src/CLAUDE.md Purpose defines profitable as '> gas + NFT cost'; the settled design decision and stories 003/005 specify gas only, so the spec contradicts itself.
findings.impactSummary: Operator/caller self-loss up to ~one NFT mint price (10-70 USD) per harvest; no third-party extraction, protocol not harmed. Story-005's own 'profitable' anvil run nets ~8.5 USD of ETH while burning a ~10.78 USDC NFT (~-2.2 USD). Break-even pending yield ~36 USD (index 1) vs script firing at ~1-2 USD.

evidence.econFork: Neither profitability gate prices the claim-NFT unit SYA burns. Fork evidence shows this is systematic, not an edge case: at the story-004/005 reference state the flagship 'profitable' full harvest pays 10.822 USD of ETH while burning NFT index 1 whose mint price is 10.783 USDC (+0.04 USD before gas, about -0.45 USD after gas at basefee+0.01 gwei; story-005's own validation 'profitable send' netted 0.00365 ETH ~ 8.5 USD against the same 10.78 USD NFT, i.e. ~-2.2 USD). A USDe-only harvest (USDC+DOLA exempt) succeeds on-chain and would be sent by harvest.sh (default MIN_PROFIT_WEI=0) paying 2.65 USD for a 10.78 USD NFT. At today's ~0.03 gwei base fee the gas floor is ~0.1-0.5 USD, so harvest.sh fires once pending yield exceeds ~1-2 USD, while the NFT-adjusted break-even is NFT/discount = 10.78/0.30 ~ 36 USD of pending yield (index 7: ~233 USD).
evidence.code: cast call 0x39Af...E10F getPrice(1) -> 10782880; dispatcher 0x9cd4...19f3b3 primeToken() -> USDC; harvest_anvil.sh case 5 'operator ETH rose by 3649871151856064 wei net of gas'.

findings.recommendation: N/A (self-inflicted loss). Mitigation: add an NFT_COST_WEI / MIN_PROFIT_WEI default derived from NFTMinterV2.getPrice(nftIndex) converted to ETH, or document that MIN_PROFIT_WEI must be set to at least the NFT's value. In harvest.sh, read nftMinter.getPrice(NFT_INDEX), convert to ETH (V4 pool slot0 or the simulated USDC/ETH rate) and add it to GAS_FLOOR; default MIN_PROFIT_WEI to that value or refuse to run without it. Document the NFT cost in the README. Owner to reconcile the spec (F-01).

findings.title: Borrow/allowance = calculateClaimAmount*1.01 with a false '~10% over-estimate' premise; DOLA runs with only 1% headroom, and over-delivery beyond it reverts the claim
findings.rootCause: Borrow buffer sized on a wrong premise (story-002 Background, repeated in NatSpec L265-268): calculateClaimAmount's over-estimate is strategy-dependent and is exact for DOLA. The 1% buffer applies to the aggregate estimate.
findings.impactSummary: Loud DoS only (SYA safeTransferFrom reverts on allowance); caller must exempt the over-delivering strategy. No loss. Story/NatSpec safety premise is factually false (Law 2).

evidence.invariantSharpening: invariant_liveness_overDelivery FAIL (adversarial, forge+medusa): USDe ~3% over estimate -> ERC20InsufficientAllowance. Tripwire refinement: the 1% buffer is on the AGGREGATE estimate, so a +2% DOLA over-delivery is absorbed in a full claim (1545.3 borrowed vs 1539 paid) but reverts in a DOLA-only claim (454.5 vs 459). Exposure is largest exactly when the caller exempts the over-estimating strategies (USDe 75%, USDC 99%) and leaves DOLA - the operator's natural reaction to other failures (e.g. DEDUP-002) removes the headroom.
evidence.symbolic: SYMBOLIC-003 (testFuzz_C6) witness: 1.28% over-delivery -> pull > borrow -> revert. SYMBOLIC-002 (testFuzz_C2): owed = est*10100/10000 floors the 1% headroom to zero for est < 100 reward-token units (< 0.0001 USDC) - dust-level sub-observation. C4 bounded fuzz: delivered_i <= estimate_i => pull <= owed (not a proof; silent on over-delivery).
evidence.patternContext: PATTERN-OBS-04 independently noted actualPayment > owed reverts loudly.

findings.recommendation: Correct story-002's premise and the NatSpec; size BORROW_BUFFER_BPS from measured worst-case delivery/estimate (per strategy, not aggregate); add a MockSYA over-delivery mode (DEDUP-010(3)).

The story's safety reasoning is false for at least one live strategy, so the 'safe direction' assurance does not hold as written. A strategy that delivers more than estimate*1.01 would revert the claim on SYA's allowance pull. That is a loud DoS, not a loss.

findings.title: Documented 'double fee' mechanism on USDe/crvUSD pool 0xF55B is wrong (opposite-direction trades, not adverse price move); direct USDe/USDC route avoids the round trip
findings.impactSummary: Cents per harvest at current sizes; caller-side profitability only. The direct USDe/USDC pool 0x0295.. noted in MainnetRoutes avoids the round trip.
findings.evidence: The documented 'double fee' on pool 0xF55B (USDe/crvUSD) is real but its stated mechanism is wrong. The live CurveAMMAdapter route for sUSDe->USDe is [sUSDe, 0x5706.., crvUSD, 0xF55B.., USDe], so the strategy skim BUYS USDe from 0xF55B (fork: pool USDe 134630.07 -> 134624.36, -5.707 USDe) and the harvester then SELLS the delivered 4.29 USDe back into the same pool (net -1.417). The trades are in opposite directions, so the first trade's price impact FAVOURS the second; the cost is two pool fees plus a needless crvUSD->USDe->crvUSD round trip, not adverse price movement. Both legs are atomic inside one tx, so no third party can insert between them.
